Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the policy. I’ll keep the candidate singular and update both required documentation files.
The skill lives under the workspace’s `guidance/skills` tree, not the attempted driver-home path. I’m correcting that and completing the contract read before inspecting images or code.

The skill requires the common prewarm sheet and rollout keyframes to be inspected before any policy edit. I’ll now anchor those visuals to the guidance, scores, observations, metrics, diagnostics, inherited notes, and the prefilled controller.

All sampled rollouts are finite successes, so there is no sampled failure to compare. I’ll use the slower, higher-effort `2.2` restoration rollout as the informative regression and compare it with the duplicated best `2.1` success, after checking the shared prewarm state.

The visuals and diagnostics agree: `2.1` self-propels upstream through the developed wake and closes on the target on a shallower, more compact path; `2.2` remains stable but turns onto a deeper route, arrives 3.87 time units later, and worsens distance, relative propulsion, effort, crossflow, force, and moment. I’m checking the inherited optimizer notes now to avoid repeating an already disproven one-dimensional gain step.

The inherited `2.05` rollout adds a useful bracket: it is the fastest and lowest-load case (`72.70`, `50630`, `21.05/379.50`) but gives up some mean-distance quality versus `2.1`. I’ll record a single falsifiable candidate that separates below-orbit recovery (`2.1`) from above-orbit dissipation (`2.05`), using only existing joint-state feedback and exact evaluated gains. This is the visual-signal skill’s required pre-edit pause.

The diagnosis and acceptance boundaries are now recorded before the controller change. I’m applying the single split-gain candidate and revising the durable energy-feedback lesson to incorporate both the inherited `2.05` tradeoff and the newly sampled `2.2` negative result.

The candidate and durable lesson are updated. I’ll now invoke the mandated checker, which will validate the parent-guidance delta, editable boundary, parameter schema, and lightweight Julia contract without running CFD.
The required guidance check passes: the notes exist and the reusable lesson is materially different from the assigned parent. I’m continuing with the non-CFD policy contract and boundary checks.

The Julia contract command could not start because this runner has no `julia` executable on `PATH`; the failure occurred before loading the candidate. I’ll still complete the mandated boundary/schema checks and look for a workspace-provided Julia launcher, without running CFD.

A Julia module is available on the runner. I’ll load that module and rerun the exact contract check; this should resolve the environment-only failure.

The inherited evaluation logs identify the installed Julia 1.12.2 runtime directly, so I can run the exact lightweight contract without the network-dependent launcher.

All three mandated checks now pass; the Julia run used the same installed 1.12.2 runtime recorded by the inherited evaluations. I’m doing one final non-CFD branch test so both the recovery and excess-energy paths are exercised, then I’ll hand off the candidate.

The extra branch test hit a transient process-launch error before Julia started; it did not expose a controller failure. I’m retrying it with the non-login shell to avoid the runner’s unrelated SSH-profile hook.

Completed exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl) splits oscillator feedback into `2.1` below-unit recovery and `2.05` above-unit dissipation.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md) records the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md) now documents the nonmonotone `2.05–2.2` evidence and future test boundary.

Guidance, parameter-schema, Julia contract, both feedback branches, and editable-boundary checks pass. No CFD was run.
